plan.estimand: Difference in means between two independent normal populations
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ vs H₁: μ₁ > μ₂ (one-sided, directional)
assumptions: Two independent normal populations with equal variances
Common SD = 7.8 dBA in both groups
scientific_notes: Metric is acoustical pressure in decibels (dBA, A-weighted)
Pooled two-sample t-test with equal variance assumption
One-sided test with alternative that treatment difference is positive
Total sample size: N = 64 participants (32 per arm)

answer.summary: For a one-sided pooled t-test comparing two independent normal means with equal variances, with n = 32 participants per group, expected mean difference δ = 4.3 dBA, common standard deviation σ = 7.8 dBA, and significance level α = 0.05, the statistical power is 0.7040583526690908 (approximately 70.41%).
answer.method: Noncentral t-distribution. Power is computed as P(t_{62} > 1.6698 | λ = 2.2051), where the noncentrality parameter λ = (δ/σ)√(n/2) = (4.3/7.8)√(32/2) = 2.2051, degrees of freedom df = 2n − 2 = 62, and the one-sided critical value is t_{62,0.95} = 1.6698. The test statistic under the alternative hypothesis follows a noncentral t-distribution with these parameters.
assumptions: Two independent normal populations with equal variances
Common standard deviation σ = 7.8 dBA in both treatment groups
Pooled variance t-test (Student's t) with equal variance assumption
No missing data or participant attrition
Balanced design with allocation ratio 1:1 (32 participants per arm)
One-sided directional hypothesis: H₁: μ₁ > μ₂
limitations: Power calculation assumes both populations are normally distributed; violations of normality may affect Type I and Type II error rates
Assumes equal variances in both groups; if variances differ substantially, Welch's t-test should be used instead
Calculation does not account for multiple comparisons if this test is part of a larger study
No adjustment for attrition or dropouts; assumes all 64 participants complete the study
Effect size (δ = 4.3 dBA) and standard deviation (σ = 7.8 dBA) are assumed known; actual power depends on accuracy of these prior specifications

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters from the user request
delta <- 4.3      # expected mean difference (dBA)
sigma <- 7.8      # common standard deviation (dBA)
n_per_group <- 32  # sample size per group
alpha <- 0.05     # significance level (one-sided)

# Effect size (standardized mean difference)
effect_size <- delta / sigma

# Calculate noncentrality parameter
# For a two-sample t-test with equal sample sizes n per group:
# λ = δ / (σ * sqrt(2/n))
# where δ is the true difference in means
noncentrality <- (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)

# Degrees of freedom for two-sample t-test
# df = n1 + n2 - 2 = 32 + 32 - 2 = 62
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
critical_value <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is P(T > critical_value | H1 is true)
# where T follows noncentral t-distribution with noncentrality parameter λ
power <- 1 - pt(critical_value, df, ncp = noncentrality)

# Create results object
results <- data.frame(
  metric = c("power", "effect_size", "noncentrality_parameter", "degrees_of_freedom", "critical_value"),
  value = c(power, effect_size, noncentrality, df, critical_value),
  unit = c("probability", "standardized_mean_difference", "noncentrality", "df", "t_value")
)

# Output as JSON
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=\n")
cat(toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "effect_size", value = round(effect_size, 15), unit = "standardized_mean_difference"),
  list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(noncentrality, 15), unit = "noncentrality"),
  list(metric = "degrees_of_freedom", value = df, unit = "df"),
  list(metric = "critical_value", value = round(critical_value, 15), unit = "t_value")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

# Print details for verification
cat("\n=== Verification Details ===\n")
cat("Mean difference (δ):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD (σ):", sigma, "dBA\n")
cat("Sample size per group (n):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", 2 * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Effect size (Cohen's d):", round(effect_size, 4), "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", round(noncentrality, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (df):", df, "\n")
cat("Critical t-value:", round(critical_value, 4), "\n")
cat("Power (1 - β):", round(power, 4), "\n")

# Evidence e1; success=true

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters from the user request
delta <- 4.3      # expected mean difference (dBA)
sigma <- 7.8      # common standard deviation (dBA)
n_per_group <- 32  # sample size per group
alpha <- 0.05     # significance level (one-sided)

# Effect size (standardized mean difference)
effect_size <- delta / sigma

# Calculate noncentrality parameter
# For a two-sample t-test with equal sample sizes n per group:
# λ = δ / (σ * sqrt(2/n))
# where δ is the true difference in means
noncentrality <- (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)

# Degrees of freedom for two-sample t-test
# df = n1 + n2 - 2 = 32 + 32 - 2 = 62
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
critical_value <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is P(T > critical_value | H1 is true)
# where T follows noncentral t-distribution with noncentrality parameter λ
power <- 1 - pt(critical_value, df, ncp = noncentrality)

# Create results object
results <- data.frame(
  metric = c("power", "effect_size", "noncentrality_parameter", "degrees_of_freedom", "critical_value"),
  value = c(power, effect_size, noncentrality, df, critical_value),
  unit = c("probability", "standardized_mean_difference", "noncentrality", "df", "t_value")
)

# Output as JSON
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=\n")
cat(toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "effect_size", value = round(effect_size, 15), unit = "standardized_mean_difference"),
  list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(noncentrality, 15), unit = "noncentrality"),
  list(metric = "degrees_of_freedom", value = df, unit = "df"),
  list(metric = "critical_value", value = round(critical_value, 15), unit = "t_value")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

# Print details for verification
cat("\n=== Verification Details ===\n")
cat("Mean difference (δ):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD (σ):", sigma, "dBA\n")
cat("Sample size per group (n):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", 2 * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Effect size (Cohen's d):", round(effect_size, 4), "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", round(noncentrality, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (df):", df, "\n")
cat("Critical t-value:", round(critical_value, 4), "\n")
cat("Power (1 - β):", round(power, 4), "\n")
